newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon - market overreacting to 15 pct income drop.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon - market overreacting to 15 pct income drop.

text.p: Raytheon Co's chief financial officer said on Monday that the 13 percent drop in his company's share price is "just the market overreacting" to Friday's news that the company will report a 15 percent drop in net operating income.
"You have to remember we were at an all-time high very recently," CFO Peter D'Angelo said in a telephone interview. "With the $50-plus range we hit trading high and a closing high."
The company's stock dropped to $46 from Thursday's $53 close.
"I've talked to a large number of our major shareholders. Yes this is a set back, a bump in the road, if you will," D'Angelo said. "But our fundamentals are strong."

Meanwhile, more than 3.4 million shares of the $12 billion industrial giant traded hands on Monday after some 5 million shares were traded Friday, representing roughly 4.0 percent of the company's outstanding stock.

The company announced on Friday that its largest unit, Raytheon Engineers & Constructor with $3 billion in revenues, had projects that were slowed because customers were unable to get financing in place.

"The power area has been a slow process that is just beginning to close," D'Angelo said on Monday. "You must remember these are not lost jobs. These are delayed jobs ... We're still expecting a E&C to be a significant growth area."
Earlier Monday, CS First Boston cut its rating to a hold and Salomon Bros removed Raytheon from its recommended large cap list.
But two other analysts in telephone interviews with Reuters said they saw the sharp drop in Raytheon's price as a buying opportunity.
"Even with the challenges and all, Raytheon in the mid-40s is a good value," said BT Securities Wolfgang Demisch, who continues to have a buy on the stock.
JSA Research, Inc analyst Paul Nisbet said, "I have it as a buy and it's even more so at this price. What we have here is a short-term phenomenon."
